subject: Follow-up: Model fit & tool-calling evals — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today — model fit & next steps

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and for walking through Acme's invoice extraction and line-item normalization use case. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can scope an eval run: 

Recap:
- Goal: extract line items (description, qty, unit_price, total, tax) and return normalized JSON that matches Acme's schema for our downstream ledger.
- Key constraints: per-document latency target of <400ms for single-file extraction, consistent JSON schema compliance, and deterministic retries for partial failures.
- Volume: ~250k docs/month, mixed PDFs and images; sample anonymized dataset ready per your note.

Initial model recommendations (based on our call):
1) Redwood-2.7b (quantized) — good latency/cost balance for baseline extraction.
2) GPT-Style-Large (open-vendor) — better structured-output accuracy on long line-item tables; recommend for quality-focused runs.
3) Fallback: Redwood-1.4b-fast — for burst/dedicated throughput where cost is primary.

Attached: redwood_benchmarks_v1.pdf (benchmarks vs expected budgets) and acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompt/ground-truth pairs we discussed).

Questions / next steps:
- Can you share a small sample set (10-20 anonymized invoices) + the exact JSON schema we need to validate against? If you prefer, a sample schema file or an endpoint spec works.
- We propose a 2-week eval: week 1 — run structured-output compliance tests (schema validation + function-calling mode), week 2 — cost/latency tuning and retry behavior tests.
- Optional: we can run a deterministic retry experiment that exercises intermittent OCR failures and our retry/backoff logic.

If that plan looks good, I'll loop in Neha (inference lead) and Aditya (solutions) for scheduling and technical onboarding. Suggest a 30-min follow-up on Monday to lock timelines.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0143

--
Attachments referenced: redwood_benchmarks_v1.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sabrina Lopez <sabrina.lopez@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — model fit & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying items before we kick off the eval: 

1) Schema: attaching the current production schema (schema_examples_acme.json) — primary requirement is strict JSON schema compliance. If the model returns any fields that don't validate, we need an explicit error/repair flow.
2) Retries/Idempotency: we need to understand retry semantics — if the model fails mid-stream or returns partial JSON, we need a deterministic retry that can resume or fail cleanly without duplicating line-items downstream. Is that something Redwood handles out of the box or will need custom orchestration?
3) OCR variability: our sample set includes low-quality scans; how do you recommend handling OCR+LLM back-to-back failures?

We can share the 15-sample anonymized set via SFTP or a secure Share link. Monday at 10am PT works for a 30-min follow-up. Sabrina (CC) is our security lead and will ask the usual compliance questions on SOC 2 and data retention.

Alex
Senior Product Manager, Acme, Inc.
alex.martinez@acme.com | (212) 555-0199

--
Attachments referenced: schema_examples_acme.json

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — model fit & next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks for the schema. Quick answers inline and a proposed plan for the Monday call (10am PT):

1) Schema compliance / repair flow:
- We recommend using Redwood's function-calling structured output mode with strict schema enforcement turned on. That will surface validation errors with an error code and the raw model output.
- For repair, we can run an automated two-pass repair flow in our eval harness: first pass attempts coercions (e.g., cast strings->numbers, normalize date formats), second pass prompts the model with the validation failure and asks to return a corrected JSON. We'll instrument and report the repair rate.

2) Retries / idempotency:
- Redwood's SDK supports idempotency keys per document and deterministic retry/backoff. For partial outputs we recommend: if function-calling returns a parse/validation error, treat as a non-idempotent failure and run the repair flow rather than blind retry.
- We'll run a deterministic retry experiment as part of week 2 to quantify duplicate avoidance under failure injection.

3) OCR variability:
- Best practice: pre-process with our recommended OCR pipeline (we can run Tesseract + layout-aware OCR or integrate your existing OCR). During the eval we'll label OCR confidence and route low-confidence pages to a higher-accuracy model variant.

Monday call agenda (10am PT):
- Quick intro (5m)
- Review schema & sample data (10m)
- Confirm eval metrics (accuracy, schema compliance %, median latency) & pass/fail thresholds (10m)
- Agree on deliverables and timeline (5m)

Action items before Monday:
- Alex: upload 15 anonymized invoices + confirm SFTP or Drive link (Sabrina, please confirm security constraints).
- Acme: confirm the exact rejection policy for failed docs (drop vs manual review).
- Redwood: we will prepare a benchmark run (Redwood-2.7b quant + GPT-Style-Large) and a proposed repair-flow script. Attachments: I uploaded benchmark primer and prompt set to the shared drive link (see links above).

If everyone is good I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short tech pre-read for Neha and Aditya.

Thanks —
Marissa

--
Attachments referenced: drive links (redwood_benchmarks_v1.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl)

Subject: Internal: Acme eval prep — schema + retry plan

Team — looping you in ahead of the Monday 10am PT call with Acme. Quick tech notes and asks so we can hit the ground running: 

- They require strict schema compliance (see attached schema_examples_acme.json). We'll run function-calling strict mode and instrument validation errors.
- Plan to run Redwood-2.7b (quant) and GPT-Style-Large in parallel for first runs. Aditya, can you spin a small benchmark job (50 docs) by EOD Tuesday? Keep latency targets in the runner so we collect median & p95.
- Neha, please outline the repair-flow prompt template and post-parse validation logic. We'll capture repair success rate and any hallucinated fields.
- Dylan, please prepare a short note on idempotency keys and our recommended SDK usage patterns to avoid duplicate line-items on retry.

I'll send the calendar invite and include the shared drive links. We'll present a short eval plan during the call and agree on deliverables.

Appreciate it —
Marissa
